To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The reaction of nitrogen with water vapour on the surface of titanium dioxide (rutile) is stimulated by near UV light.
(1) Molecular nitrogen can be photochemically converted into ammonia by near UV radiation on the surface of a photocatalyst.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel process for the fixation of molecular nitrogen in the soil, using near UV light.

the development of a photocatalytic process which will fix atmospheric nitrogen into ammonia and hydrazilne in the presence of a suitable catalyst and water vapour, under the stimulus of low-energy UV radiation, at room temperature.
the development of new photocatalytic materials for the reduction of nitrogen to ammonia and hydride compounds.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
molecular nitrogen can be fixed on the surface of TiO2 in the presence of low energy UV radiation and water vapour to form hydrazine and ammonia, the latter being the major product.

(i) Molecular nitrogen can be fixed on the surface of TiO2 by near UV radiation, (ii) The reaction is catalytic, (iii) The reaction is not catalysed by visible light, (iv) The rate of reaction depends on the surface area of TiO2, (v) The reaction is inhibited by molecular nitrogen in excess of that required for saturation of the TiO2, but is not inhibited by the presence of molecular oxygen.
the reaction is a surface process, and the mechanism is a photochemical reduction of molecular nitrogen to hydrazine, which is subsequently oxidised to ammonia.

the fixation of molecular nitrogen is a photochemical process which is catalysed by a transition-metal oxide.
